title: Prove an ordinary four-cycle costs ten with restored donors (no κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped written proof with an exact finite exclusion certificate, produced by Nick Petalas. The ordinary four-cycle `(x0,x1,x2,x3) -> (x1,x2,x3,x0)` costs exactly **ten scalar primitives**, with any finite number of arbitrary dirty donors restored individually.

```text
cycle-write reduction: at most two written donors in a nine-step word
six-register F3 endpoint: no word through length nine
literal rational upper word: ten operations
exact scalar boundary price: ten
```

The alphabet is distinct-register ADD/SUB, NEG, DOUBLE/HALVE, COPY and CLEAR, with no free signs, renamings, clean allocation or discarded coordinates. The new step is the ordinary-four-cycle endpoint exclusion and its unbounded-donor consequence. Credit Philipp / mightyOil #1303 for the cycle-sensitive reduction and two metric-ball engines, and Ross Richardson #1216/#1145 for the restored-donor model, specialization, modular method and elementary templates. Their original permutation results are cited, not replayed. The package retains all predecessor credit and changes no predecessor source.

## Evidence

Each of the two source-credited native representations enumerates 2,299,917 matrices and minimum distances and checks all 151,794,522 middle transitions for the new endpoint `123045`. Both find zero direct and zero middle hits. Full canonical matrix/distance streams agree byte for byte. The ten-operation rational word and its inverse agree on all six independent input columns; all ten single-operation omissions are rejected.

An independently represented dense 48-state control ball agrees with both engines at three small endpoints. Both engines reject two malformed native domains for their declared reasons, and six damaged endpoint reports are rejected. Warning-strict normal and optimized replays produce identical receipts bound to all five package files and four live sources.

Local checks passed on CPython 3.12.15 and Clang 21.0.0, build clang-2100.4.1.1, targeting arm64-apple-darwin27.0.0. Each registered command takes about 22 seconds locally; the combined registered replay took 45.07 seconds. Exact reproduction commands from the repository root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/restored-unsigned-four-cycle
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/restored-unsigned-four-cycle --check-source-history --check-modes
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/restored-unsigned-four-cycle/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -O -W error -B research/restored-unsigned-four-cycle/verify.py
```

A C++17 compiler named `c++` with `unsigned __int128` support is required. Both native engines compile with `-Wall -Wextra -Werror`. Package metadata/pins, exact committed bytes/modes and declared source ancestry pass. The official nine-file export passes integrity and declared-input coverage checks. An optimized replay of the read-only Git-free export also passes.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

This is an exact scalar boundary price. No current native four-cycle caller, paid recursive improvement, physical frame/tape layout, supplier admission or new kappa is claimed. Selected #7000 is unchanged. Promised inputs, clean/disposable workspace, arbitrary scalar multipliers, free monomial maps, joint complex-component arithmetic, nonlinear gates and changed composite boundaries are outside this model. Full supplier, precision, hosting, compiler and outer-theorem obligations were not run. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

## Open next questions

- Can an actual four-cycle boundary and an adjacent scalar run be synthesized below ten? First pin the complete caller map, frame and ownership ledger; that caller is not supplied here.
- Can a write-pattern or support invariant replace this finite metric-ball exclusion while retaining arbitrary mixed rows? A complete symbolic certificate is missing. No larger permutation search is part of this contribution.

## Related open work

No other open PR identified for this exact ordinary arithmetic four-cycle endpoint. The source #1303 is merged.

- [#7552](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7552) studies the minimum boundary-inclusive scalar bill under global integer dyadic gauges; this result fixes a permutation endpoint in the declared unit-price arithmetic alphabet.
- [#7547](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7547) studies source insertion with a restored dirty spare; this result prices a closed four-cycle endpoint. Its ADD upper bound and this exact permutation price are different quantities.

## CI notes

**CI did not execute or certify this package.** At unchanged head `66e05cf6c6058cff8a41a9b3ebe5945f5e36e9be`, [run 43522890842](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/43522890842), [plan job 132221300900](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/43522890842/job/132221300900), failed in `Onboarding helper tests`. The log reports 760 tests, exactly one failure and 24 skipped. The sole failing test is `test_research_current_status.CurrentCiNavigationTests.test_current_ci_section_matches_selected_record`, at line 58. Its AssertionError says that '`make frontier7000-verify`' was not found in the CI verification document.

The repository-level mismatch is present in base main `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`: `certificates/selected-result.json` names `make frontier7000-verify`, while the current section of `docs/ci-verification.md` describes #6030 and `make frontier6030-verify`. Those files and `tests/test_research_current_status.py` are unchanged by this PR. The dependent [replay job 132223031757](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/43522890842/job/132223031757) was skipped. The local evidence above is therefore not hosted CI certification.

I independently inspected the logs of rohanarun's [run 42905094314, plan job 130140894651](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/42905094314/job/130140894651) and dillona's [run 42903313790, plan job 130134720799](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/42903313790/job/130134720799). Both show the same sole failing test, assertion, 760-test count and 24 skips; both dependent replay jobs are skipped. No claim is made here about other runs whose logs were not inspected.

No code fix, retrigger commit or job rerun was made for this repository-level failure.

## Merge danger

Two-way door. Blast radius: isolated research package. Only five new package files are added; shared code, frozen sources and the selected frontier are unchanged.
